$comment: No standalone validation-rules.json structure was ever drafted in the frozen architecture (Architecture '4. Stage 4...md' has ~40 example rules in prose plus full per-category obligation lists, but never a worked data file). This file's shape (id/category/provenance/mandatory/description/validation_stage) is a COMPLETED construction. Rule content is EXTRACTED where an architecture citation is given; rules marked provenance=COMPLETED extend an explicitly-described category/obligation into a discrete, numbered rule the architecture itself did not enumerate. See docs/development/contract-v1-completion-log.md for the full review.

categories.RC-CON: Contract/schema resolution — is the declared Contract version real and usable
categories.RC-REPRO: Reproducibility — structural equivalence across independently generated candidate Releases built from identical inputs

validation_order_note: EXTRACTED — Architecture '4. Stage 4...md' Sec 9.5: Contract availability -> Release-root accessibility -> directory structure -> manifest parsing -> manifest schema validation -> cross-field identity validation -> declared-path validation -> artifact validation -> script validation -> configuration validation -> database validation -> offline-dependency validation -> security validation -> integrity preparation -> compliance decision -> Compliance Report generation. RC-REPRO is deliberately excluded from this sequence and from validation_order above: every other category validates ONE candidate Release in isolation; RC-REPRO-001 requires comparing TWO independently generated candidate Releases built from identical inputs, which `rah validate` cannot do against a single already-built Release. It is a build-time regression check (run by re-invoking the Packager twice against the same fixture inputs), not a step in the per-Release compliance decision.
outcome_states_note: EXTRACTED — Architecture Sec 9.8. NOT_APPLICABLE = a conditional rule whose trigger doesn't apply; must record why, shall not be used to hide missing mandatory information. NOT_EXECUTED = could not be evaluated due to an earlier fatal failure. Overall Compliance Report result stays binary PASS/FAIL (Sec 9.2) — a rule-level NOT_APPLICABLE or NOT_EXECUTED never itself becomes the overall result.
compliance_decision_rule: COMPLIANT only if every applicable mandatory rule passes, none fail, no required rule stays NOT_EXECUTED, final integrity closure succeeds, and the Compliance Report generates successfully. A warning shall not change compliance unless the Contract identifies that warning condition as mandatory failure. (EXTRACTED — Architecture Sec 9.20.) COMPLETED: no rule below is marked non-mandatory ("warning") — the architecture names the concept but never identifies a specific rule as warning-level, so this Contract version treats every listed rule as mandatory. Revisit if a future need for warning-level rules arises.
fatal_failure_rule: EXTRACTED — Architecture Sec 9.6. Fatal (validator MAY stop dependent checks): Release root inaccessible, release.yaml missing, YAML unparseable, Contract version unresolved. All other failures are non-fatal and shall NOT stop unrelated checks — the Validator should continue and report every discoverable violation in one run.

rules.description: compatibility.release_contract_version resolves to a published, existing Contract version directory (e.g. contracts/1.0/).
The Manifest's manifest_schema_version is one the resolved Contract version supports. The Generator/Validator shall not mix rules from multiple Contract versions.
Release root directory naming is valid: <ApplicationName>_Release_<SemanticVersion>, matching release.yaml's application.name and release.version.
Exactly one authoritative release.yaml exists at Release root.
All mandatory Release directories exist: compose/, docker-images/, scripts/, configuration/, documentation/, verification/, checksums/, compliance/, and database/ when database.required=true.
All mandatory Release files exist within their required directories (compose/docker-compose.yml, checksums/SHA256SUMS).
No two lifecycle scripts are declared for the same deployment.entrypoints operation (no duplicate lifecycle scripts).
No required checksum resource is missing.
Every declared relative path is valid (resolves inside Release root).
No forbidden absolute path is used outside the explicit deployment.canonical_path exception.
No path traversal (../) appears in any declared path.
No unknown or repurposed reserved directory/file name is present.
release.yaml validates against release-manifest.schema.json.
application.name and application.slug match Project Version State.
release.version matches the selected project version and the Release directory name.
source.git_tag, when present, corresponds to release.version.
deployment.canonical_path corresponds to application.slug (/opt/rah/apps/<slug>).
deployment.compose_project_name is stable and version-independent (does not contain the Release version).
The Validator rejects unsupported YAML tags or executable constructs in release.yaml before schema validation.
Every required Docker image archive declared under docker.images exists at its declared archive path.
Every required documentation file declared under documentation exists.
Every required verification artifact declared under verification exists.
Every declared deployment.entrypoints value exists as a real file inside scripts/.

Every models.artifacts[] entry (when models.required=true) declares a baked_into_image value matching a real entry in docker.images[].service. COMPLETED: adapted from the architecture's original 'model artifact packaged_path must exist' rule to this project's bake-into-image policy.
Every Docker image declared in docker.images[] is referenced by compose/docker-compose.yml.
Declared Manifest contents match the actual packaged files byte-for-byte at the declared identity (no drift between what release.yaml claims and what is physically present).
Each Docker image archive is inspectable, contains the declared image name/tag, and is not empty or malformed. The Validator is not required to run the image.
Every declared lifecycle script exists.
Every lifecycle script is located inside scripts/.
Every lifecycle script referenced by deployment.entrypoints is declared in release.yaml (no undeclared scripts silently relied upon).

install entrypoint is declared and exists when supported_operations.fresh_install=true; update entrypoint when supported_operations.update=true; backup entrypoint when database.backup_before_update.required=true.
Every declared script has executable permissions and passes a static syntax check (e.g. bash -n). The Validator shall not perform a real install, update, recovery, or production migration.
If supported_operations.downgrade=false, no script or manifest declaration implies the Platform may treat an older version as directly deployable over a newer one.
deployment.transition declarations are non-empty when supported_operations.update=true, unless an explicit 'any previous version' policy is declared.
configuration/ templates contain no production secrets.
Every input the Platform-facing configuration template requires is declared under configuration.inputs.
Each configuration.inputs[] entry has a valid type, and operator/generated/platform/fixed source values are internally consistent (e.g. a 'generated' input does not also declare a fixed default).
Inputs of type 'port' use a valid port-shaped default when a default is present; secret-typed inputs do not carry a real default value.
Required database artifacts exist when database.required=true.
Migration entrypoints exist when database.migration.required_for_update=true and supported_operations.update=true.

database.platform and database.deployment_mode are declared when database.required=true; target_schema_version is declared; backup/recovery resources exist when database.backup_before_update.required=true.
The Validator does not execute a real production migration while validating database resources.

offline_requirements.public_internet_required, public_registry_required, public_cdn_required, and online_model_registry_required are all false. A Release declaring any of these true shall not be accepted.
rules.architecture_reference: 4. Stage 4...md Sec 29 items 22-23, Sec 23-24 (offline_requirements field spec)

rules.description: Every required Docker image is available offline within docker-images/ — no mandatory runtime image requires a public pull.
Every required model artifact is packaged (baked into a declared Docker image) or supplied by an approved RAH-OIP offline capability — none depends on an online model registry.

No undeclared public Internet, registry, package-repository, CDN, model-registry, or externally-downloaded frontend-asset dependency is present anywhere in the Release. An undeclared required external dependency results in non-compliance.
No real production password appears anywhere in release.yaml.
No unapproved private key is embedded in the Release.
configuration.inputs[] entries marked secret:true carry no real value in release.yaml or configuration/ templates; password-type defaults are normally null.
No generated secret appears in the Manifest — generated secrets belong to post-deployment operational state, not the Release.
No declared path or script escapes the Release root, and no manifest field contains executable content in a data field or an unsupported/dangerous construct.
Validator output never prints a complete secret value, even when reporting a security-rule failure.
checksums/SHA256SUMS exists.
Every critical artifact (release.yaml, artifacts, scripts, documentation, verification resources, the Compliance Report) is represented in SHA256SUMS. SHA256SUMS shall not list itself.
The recorded manifest checksum matches release.yaml's actual contents.

Integrity closure follows the two-stage bootstrapping sequence: (A) validate everything except final SHA256SUMS and the Compliance Report, (B) generate the Compliance Report, then generate the final SHA256SUMS covering it, then verify the final checksum file, then freeze. This rule supersedes any simplified description implying checksums are generated before the Compliance Report without this closure step.

Given the same application, target version, source Git commit, validated engineering answers, and Packaging Software version, two independently generated candidate Releases shall be structurally equivalent: identical directory structure; identical script, configuration, documentation, and database resource content by checksum; identical declared Docker image identity (service/repository/tag) in release.yaml. Excluded from equivalence, as fields inherently unique per build execution: release.created_at, the Compliance Report's generated_at, and any checksum or content that transitively depends on those timestamps. Known limitation, not asserted by this rule: byte-for-byte Docker image archive content equality, since that depends on whether the underlying `docker build` process is itself reproducible, which is outside the Packager's control.
rules.architecture_reference: Promoted from docs/development/Period A — Independent Product Development; Packager/1. Initial GPT Proposal.md P6 'Reproducibility' test. Architecture Sec 11.1 names reproducibility as a goal but never operationalized it into a rule — this is the first concrete definition.
